document_metadata.title: 2、INT. BARRY'S WAREHOUSE - THAT MOMENT
document_metadata.summary: Barry takes in a street piano after Lena leaves; he tests it in his office, producing a faint note, and becomes absorbed in its fragile sound.

chunks.content: Barry is on the phone, speaking hesitantly as he tries to clarify details with the other person. The voice on the line asks about the material of an unspecified object—whether it’s plastic and what happens if it breaks. Barry confirms it’s plastic, but seems uncertain about the implications. The caller assures him they’ll run the numbers and call back first thing tomorrow. Barry, concerned about the time difference, asks if the caller has his home number in case of an early call, but the caller dismisses the need, stating they have his work number. After a brief exchange, they say their goodbyes. Barry hangs up and steps outside, the camera following him into the alley. He pauses, gazing down the alley at a piano—later identified as a Harmonium—sitting in the street. The quiet moment is interrupted as a small Ford Escort pulls into the driveway, maneuvering around the Harmonium and parking. Lena Leonard, a young woman, exits the car and walks toward Barry. The camera shifts to a two-shot profile as she greets him and asks if he works at the mechanic’s shop. Barry replies that he doesn’t, and informs her the shop doesn’t open until eight. She seems slightly flustered, having thought it opened earlier, and asks if it would be alright to leave her car there. Barry repeatedly responds that he doesn’t know, explaining he doesn’t know the mechanics well. Lena then asks if she can trust him to hold her keys and pass them on when the mechanics arrive. After a brief hesitation, Barry agrees.

metadata.title: 2、INT. BARRY'S WAREHOUSE - THAT MOMENT

chunks.content: Lena confirms the location of her parked car, and Barry assures her it should be fine. She hands him the keys, and as she turns to leave, she notices the piano in the street. Barry acknowledges it with a simple 'Yeah.' After a beat, Lena thanks him, suggests she might see him later when picking up her car, and walks away. Barry begins to return inside the warehouse but pauses, watching her. Just before she exits the alley, Lena glances back over her shoulder, prompting Barry to quickly duck out of sight. The camera holds on the empty alley for a moment before Barry reemerges, looking first at the Harmonium, then around the quiet street. After a moment of contemplation, he walks over to the instrument and picks it up, carrying it back toward his workspace. He brings the Harmonium into his office and sets it on his desk. Tentatively, he presses a few keys, but no sound comes out. He then steps on the foot pedal and tries again—this time, a faint note emerges. He repeats the action, holding the note as a beat passes, absorbed in the small, fragile sound.
